title: Guaranteed constraint satisfaction in generation
bottleneck: There is no general way to guarantee that a model's output satisfies hard constraints — no disallowed content, valid syntax, physical feasibility — because generation is probabilistic token sampling, not constraint solving. Post-hoc filters catch common violations but can be bypassed, and constrained decoding only handles simple formal constraints. For open-ended constraints like not revealing a secret, guarantees don't exist. Larger models memorize more, and deduplication at web scale is imperfect, so sensitive strings slip through training.
why_it_blocks: Regulated and safety-critical applications need guarantees, not best efforts. A 99.9% compliance rate still means thousands of violations at scale. A single memorized credential or medical record in outputs can trigger liability no usefulness offsets.
current_state: Guardrails and classifiers are layered atop models; researchers acknowledge they reduce but cannot guarantee safe outputs.

sources.title: The Persistence of Vulnerability: Unsolved Challenges in Artificial Intelligence Risk Management (2016–2026)
